scope: 2026 retention geography for James W. Campanella and Chris Hitzemann following the division of the old Twentieth Judicial Circuit
finding: The site's current Twenty-Fourth Circuit county set is supported: Monroe, Perry, Randolph and Washington. Both judges appear in official current-election publication ballots in all four counties. The official East St. Louis specimen, a St. Clair County election jurisdiction, includes Barberis appellate retention but neither circuit judge. No production correction is indicated for these two records.

legalContext.finding: The Act split the old Twentieth Circuit on December 5, 2022: St. Clair became the Twentieth, while Monroe, Perry, Randolph and Washington became the Twenty-Fourth. It assigned the four counties' resident judgeships to the new circuit. Section 37 preserves pre-enactment judges' choice of old or new circuit for retention. Therefore the administrative map alone cannot establish a particular incumbent's retention electorate; current election documents were checked.
legalContext.access: Full official public-act HTML read through web tool. Current compiled-statute full-page direct retrieval returned 403/502; current indexed section37 text agrees on the old/new retention choice, but is not treated as a separate full-text review.

limits: No signed individual declaration selecting the retention district was obtained; current official specimens provide direct evidence of the ballots actually published.
The conclusion is specific to these two 2026 records. It must not be generalized to another incumbent merely from a current court map.
